ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. B-9, ss. 15.1–15.4 (unlimited liability corporations) and the register of individuals with significant control provisions; Investment Canada Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 28 (1st Supp.) requiring a notification for the establishment of a new Canadian business by a non-Canadian; FINTRAC guidance applicable to low-risk e-commerce merchants.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport (proof of identity) for each incorporator, director, officer and any 25%+ significant control individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for apostille-member states) OR Consular Legalization (for non-apostille jurisdictions), followed by certified English or French translation if not issued in English/French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of certificate of incorporation and good standing for any non-resident corporate shareholder of the Alberta ULC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization plus certified translation where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for incorporation capital verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Deposit-taking financial institution of the funding shareholder or principal

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized execution (jurat); no apostille required for internally generated Canadian documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation AML/CFT screening: (i) PEP screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against FINTRAC-supported PEP classifications including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and PEP relatives/close associates; (ii) sanctions screening against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Canadian SEMA sanctions list, and, where relevant, EU and UK consolidated lists; (iii) FATF high-risk jurisdiction enhanced due diligence for any funding counterparty situated in listed jurisdictions; (iv) STR/TSTR obligations to FINTRAC for unusual activity or inconsistencies; and (v) transaction-level screening of Kickstarter, Stripe, and PayPal counterparties for embargoed-country IP addresses, blocked persons, and prohibited methods of payment. All AML/CFT records, including UBO registers and screening results, must be retained for a minimum of five years. The business is classified Low_Risk_Standard for banking AML purposes, but cross-border prepaid crowdfunding flows require continuous monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Government of Alberta: alberta.ca/corporate-registry) using the mandatory NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) pre-clearance and submission through an authorized Alberta corporate registry agent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate legal names in Alberta must be expressed in English or French using Latin alphabet characters; French-language statutory elements are permitted (e.g., 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' for a ULC). There is no statutory transliteration requirement for Canadian Indigenous or non-Latin scripts; any foreign-language trade name must be transliterated or translated into English or French for the registered legal name. For an unlimited liability corporation, the name must end with the element 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'. The name must be distinguishable from existing Alberta and federal corporate names and must not mislead as to legal form, purpose, or government connection.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Co-operative (Co-op) — requires enrolment under the Co-operative Associations Act
Any token implying ministerial approval, royal charter, or sovereign sponsorship
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, Alberta Corporate Registry issues a written refusal with reasons. The applicant may (i) file a fresh NUANS search and reserve an amended distinguishable name, or (ii) within 30 days of the refusal, submit a formal reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registry, Alberta Corporate Registries, setting out the grounds for distinctiveness and eligibility, attaching the refusal notice, the NUANS report, and any written consent letters obtained from provincial ministers or regulatory bodies for sensitive tokens. The Director typically responds within 30–45 days. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. Authorized registry agents may charge a nominal service fee for resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the statutory registered office provided the Alberta ULC maintains a physical service-of-process address in Alberta and a licensed registered agent accepts documents. Because the underlying commercial activity is physical epoxy-resin polyhedral dice casting, a separate operational premises (home studio or light-industrial unit) will be required for production, fire safety, municipal zoning, and consumer chemical product compliance. Virtual offices are generally accepted by Stripe, PayPal, and Kickstarter subject to the platform's own address verification and identity checks; a manual review hold may apply until an operating address is confirmed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5–10% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection). Inspection exposure primarily arises from municipal fire and building code enforcement and Health Canada consumer chemical product safety (CCPSA) regimes rather than corporate registry audits. FINTRAC examinations are desk-based and risk-triggered; no routine physical inspection is anticipated for this low-risk e-commerce manufacturing classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (as amended), ss 6-10 (incorporation, Certificate of Incorporation), ss 15-16 (share capital and unlimited liability), s 12 (registered office), ss 101-121 (directors and officers); Corporate Names Regulation, Alta Reg 276/2000.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta / RegistryXpress, Government of Alberta, Edmonton, Alberta, Canada.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under the ABCA) together with a preamble NUANS corporate name search report; the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation as the constitutive instrument. The name suffix 'ULC' or the phrase 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' is mandatory where unlimited shareholder liability is adopted.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the ABCA; no minimum authorized paid-up capital, no escrow deposit account requirement, and no statutory paid-in capital probationary period. Shares may be issued at nominal par value; consideration must be fully received and deposited in the corporate bank account prior to certificate issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Board accepts the subscription for the Corporation's authorized ULC common shares and preferred shares from founding subscribers; shares shall be issued upon receipt of full consideration. (2) The registered office is established at [street address], [city], Alberta, and signing officers are directed to file the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors with the Alberta Corporate Registry. (3) The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary. (4) Officers are authorized to execute all filings, open banking accounts, and obtain municipal and environmental permits in furtherance of the epoxy resin dice manufacturing business, effective upon the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / RegistryXpress online portal (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) corporate name inspection request through an approved RegistryXpress service provider for the proposed name ending in 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'. Reserve the approved name for 90 days. Provide a disambiguation statement where the name is arguably similar to an existing trademark or corporate name. If a numbered company is preferred, proceed with a sequential registration number reserved by the Registry.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and name components
NUANS name search request form and fee receipt
Disambiguation letter or consent from the holder of a conflicting name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised NUANS request with alternative names; seek a formal reconsideration by the Registrar under Alta Reg 276/2000; or incorporate under a numbered name and subsequently amend the articles to add a trade name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation on Form 1 of the ABCA, including the corporate name, registered office address in Alberta, share structure (Class A voting common shares and Class B non-voting preferred shares), restrictions on transfers, and the unlimited liability clause. The Articles must be signed by a subscriber. E-file the Articles and paying the CAD 200 statutory filing fee via RegistryXpress or a registered agent. The Certificate of Incorporation is issued electronically upon approval.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
NUANS name search report (not older than 90 days)
Consent to act as director, executed by each initial director
Organizer/subscriber signature pages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or deficiency notice, respond with corrected Articles through RegistryXpress within 30 days; if the Articles are rejected, re-file with amended provisions; an appeal of a Registrar's decision may be brought to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Initial Registry Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, file the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors under the ABCA using the RegistryXpress system. Confirm that the registered office is situated in Alberta and that at least one director is an Alberta resident or, alternatively, that an attorney for service has been appointed. Obtain certified corporate extracts and assemble the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notice of Registered Office (Form 2)
Notice of Directors (Form 3)
Consent to act as director(s)
Attestation of registered office address, if non-owner leased office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the rejected filing and re-file via RegistryXpress promptly; for late filings, submit a signed declaration of voluntary late filing under the same registry; if the registered office confirmation is disputed, provide a lease agreement or landlord consent letter to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Share Subscriptions, and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary (internal corporate governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting; adopt General Operating Bylaw No. 1; ratify the first board resolution covering registered office, officer appointments, banking resolutions, and share issuance; issue share certificates to founding subscribers; register share transfers and beneficial ownership in the share register; appoint a corporate secretary to complete minute book and register filings.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Bylaw No. 1 (General Operating Bylaw)
Organization and share subscription resolutions
Share certificates and share register
Register of Directors and Officers
Registered office and records address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If share issuance was improperly completed, the Board may pass a rectifying resolution and reissue certificates; any deficient bylaw may be adopted as an interim bylaw and ratified at the first annual shareholder meeting; if records are lost, file a correction application with the Registrar for certified re-issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, Development Permit, and Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Office (City of Edmonton / City of Calgary) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence and a development/building permit for the craft manufacturing studio; confirm zoning permits light-industrial manufacturing. Register the Corporation with the CRA for a nine-digit Business Number (BN), GST/HST account (mandatory after CAD 30,000 revenue threshold), and payroll account; obtain provincial corporate income tax account registration with the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application form
Development permit / building permit application and floor layout
Certificate of Incorporation and registered office details
CRA Business Number online registration information
Zoning compliance confirmation from municipal planning department
Lease agreement or ownership proof of the manufacturing premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is denied due to zoning, light-industrial-use or fire safety concerns, appeal the decision to the Municipal Subdivision and Development Appeal Board (MSDAB); for CRA queries, submit the Certificate of Incorporation and a corporate resolution identifying the authorized signatory; escalate unresolved taxation issues to the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration or CRA Objections Branch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) – Environmental Regulatory Approvals Division; Alberta Municipal Affairs – Safety Services Directorate (Fire and Building); Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) under the Alberta OHS Act; Municipal Planning Department of the City of [Edmonton/Calgary].
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: EPEA Registration or Exemption Confirmation for Small-Scale Resin Casting Operations; Alberta Fire Code Occupancy Permit; Municipal Development Permit and Business Licence; OHS Hazard Assessment Workplace Clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), Environmental Regulatory Approvals Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Registration level (small-scale artisanal craft manufacturing). Registration under the Activities Designation Regulation (Alta Reg 278/2003) is required if manufacturing capacity or waste release thresholds are exceeded; otherwise an Exemption Confirmation letter is obtained. Conversion to a full EPEA Approval (equivalent to an EIA) is triggered only when annual VOC emissions exceed 10 tonnes or hazardous waste generation exceeds provincial registration thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to municipal sewer must meet City of Edmonton Bylaw C-506 or equivalent municipal standards: pH 6.0-11.0, temperature ≤ 55°C, TSS ≤ 200 mg/L, COD ≤ 450 mg/L, and no free-standing uncured epoxy resin in aqueous effluent. Airborne emissions: localized ventilation control to maintain worker VOC exposure below 0.5 kg per kg of resin applied and annual facility VOC release below 2.0 tonnes; compliance with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (CEPA) SMOC for volatile organic compounds. Hazardous waste: uncured resin, hardener, acetone/isopropyl alcohol wash stills and contaminated PPE must be segregated, stored in sealed DOT-approved containers, and transported by a licensed hazardous waste carrier under the Waste Control Regulation (Alta Reg 192/1996); Environmental Quality Guidelines for Alberta Surface Waters apply for any accidental spill containment response or discharge of treated effluent to land or water.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification: municipal fire inspector inspection and issuance of an occupancy permit under the Alberta Fire Code (Alta Reg 31/2018), including compliant storage of Class IB flammable liquids in approved flammable liquid safety cabinets and cooling/curing area separation. Structural load clearance: municipal building official report confirming floor load capacity sufficient for resin casting stations, UV curing racks and polyhedral mould inventory, together with issuance of a building occupancy certificate. Occupational clearance: completion of a workplace hazard assessment under the Alberta OHS Code (Alta Reg 87/2009), incorporation of WHMIS 2015 safety data sheets and labelling for epoxy resins and solvents, installation of local exhaust ventilation, provision and documented use of personal protective equipment, and submission of an employer chemical exposure remediation plan to Alberta Occupational Health and Safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), acting for the Minister of National Revenue. Primary federal registration portal: Business Registration Online (BRO) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html. Alberta's corporate registry is Service Alberta / Corporate Registry; Alberta corporate income tax is administered and collected by CRA through the federal T2 corporate return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Following Alberta incorporation, the ULC must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN). Canadian-resident corporations normally apply online through Business Registration Online; non-resident-owned or newly formed Alberta ULCs may submit Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' or, where the corporation has no Canadian address or is a non-resident registrant, Form RC2 'Request for a Business Number - Non-Resident'. The BN is the national taxpayer identifier; a separate GST/HST program account is created when the ULC registers for GST/HST. CRA imposes no minimum capital requirement for ULC formation, and non-resident ownership is permitted under Alberta law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (cross-border label): for Canadian CRA income tax purposes, an Alberta ULC is a taxable corporation resident in Canada and cannot be characterized as a partnership; however, it is not a per se corporation under the U.S. check-the-box rules, so a single-member ULC may be disregarded or treated as a partnership for U.S. federal tax purposes only.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic 'check-the-box' election. An Alberta ULC may file IRS Form 8832 to elect U.S. classification as a corporation, partnership, or disregarded entity, but that U.S. election does not override Canadian entity-level taxation. Canada does not offer a unilateral election to cure hybrid mismatches; hybrid mismatch outcomes are addressed through treaty tie-breaker and Canadian statutory rules, and the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention does not automatically reclassify a Canadian-resident ULC as fiscally transparent unless the relevant income is treated as such under both treaty and domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax), imposed under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. Alberta has no provincial sales tax or HST, so only the 5% federal GST applies to taxable supplies made in or imported into Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, measured in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters (the 'small supplier' threshold). A Canadian-resident ULC exceeding CAD 30,000 in taxable revenues must register and charge GST. Non-residents carrying on business in Canada or soliciting taxable supplies through remote/digital channels may also be subject to registration at the same CAD 30,000 threshold, with specific rules for digital services and non-resident vendors.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscal e-invoicing, API transaction clearance, or digital tax stamping. CRA accepts standard electronic invoices and supports electronic records, but there is no national clearance portal. Exporters must retain GST/HST books, invoices, shipping records, and export declarations for six years from the end of the relevant fiscal year and must provide CRA with records in machine-readable format upon request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant supplying tangible personal property (such as handcrafted epoxy resin polyhedral dice sets) may apply the 0% rate under Part V, Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act when the supplier ships the goods through a common carrier or exporter to a destination outside Canada, or delivers them to an authorized export agent and export actually occurs. The supplier must obtain and retain contemporaneous documentary proof of export, issue a zero-rated invoice, and file the GST/HST return reflecting the zero-rated supply. Incidental design/customization services provided to non-residents may also be zero-rated where they are physically delivered outside Canada or performed for a non-resident who is outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Customs Export Declaration, Form B13A or electronic Canada Export Reporting System (CAED) record, where the export value or commodity requires CBSA export reporting; low-value parcel exports may be documented through the courier's or postal operator's electronic export manifest
Bill of lading, air waybill, or recognized courier waybill identifying the seller, the overseas destination, and delivery terms such as FOB, EXW, or DAP
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the dice products, quantity, unit price, total export consideration, and foreign buyer

Proof of payment or foreign remittance, including bank transfer advice, credit card/PayPal/Kickstarter settlement reports, or equivalent payment records; Canada does not issue statutory 'inward remittance certificates', but CRA accepts equivalent documentary evidence of settlement in a foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may retroactively disallow export zero-rating, reassess the supply as taxable at 5%, deny or claw back input tax credits and refunds, and impose interest and penalties if the exporter cannot substantiate export with complete documentary evidence. Under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act, knowing or gross-negligent false statements in returns, invoices, or export documentation attract civil penalties equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the resulting tax understatement or false refund. Deliberate export fraud can be prosecuted as tax evasion under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act, carrying fines of up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years on indictment; the normal four-year reassessment limitation period does not apply where there is misrepresentation or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential regulation of deposit-taking institutions is discharged by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing supervision is discharged by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); economic sanctions administration and enforcement is shared by Global Affairs Canada and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a free-floating, fully convertible Canadian dollar (CAD). Neither the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) nor the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2) imposes exchange controls, prior authorization, or repatriation licenses on current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit remittance from an Alberta ULC to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted; the only statutory charge is Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (25% statutory, typically reduced to 5%-15% under the Canada-U.S. Income Tax Convention), which the payer bank does not enforce as a treasury control. Goods, services, and crowdfunding settlements (Kickstarter/Stripe) may freely enter and leave Canada in CAD or foreign currency. The capital account is equally open for equity injections, shareholder loans, and intercompany trade payables, subject only to FINTRAC large-transaction reporting and OSFI prudential rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline exist in Canada. The wartime Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1952, and contemporary law does not obligate exporters to sell foreign currency to the Bank of Canada or to a chartered bank. Proceeds from exports of handcrafted dice (HS 9504.40, NAICS 339930) may be held indefinitely in CAD, USD, or foreign-currency accounts. The only reporting obligations are (a) FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Reports for cash transactions of CAD 10,000 or more, (b) FINTRAC Cross-Border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reports for physical movements of CAD 10,000+ (E677), and (c) customary SWIFT message archival at the clearing bank. No central-bank conversion license is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account with dedicated USD account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability is conditional: offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise Platform, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) are usable as secondary payout and FX-conversion rails, but not as the primary treasury account for a Canadian ULC. They are generally registered as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC rather than as Schedule I or II chartered banks; balances are not CDIC-insured; and they cannot issue documentary credits or guarantee instruments. Once the Retail Payment Activities Act is fully in force, a Platform Payment Service Provider with a FINTRAC MSB registration may clear CAD but remains outside the Payments Canada settlement system for SWIFT-based trade finance. Legal constraints include PCMLTFA MSB registration (sections 50A-50G), provincial consumer-protection licensing where applicable, and heightened account-reviews for high-velocity e-commerce flows. The recommendation is to operate the EMI as a re-currency bridge for Kickstarter/Stripe receipts only, with a same-day sweep to a tier-1 chartered bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical branch visit for at least one director or authorized signatory is the de facto requirement at tier-1 Canadian banks, though it is not a strict statutory mandate. PCMLTFA client due diligence requires verification of identity by a credible government-issued photo document; it permits remote verification through notarization or video if the financial institution's risk-approach is sound. In practice: (a) a Canadian resident director can open a low-risk sole-shareholder business account fully online at RBC, TD, or BMO using a notary or video verification; (b) for a non-resident director or shareholder, most tier-1 banks require (i) an in-person visit to an Alberta branch, or (ii) a certified true copy of the passport, a notarized household address proof, an apostilled board resolution, and a subsequent telephone or video compliance interview. The recommended treasury action is to appoint a Canadian resident director or authorized signatory and, where possible, physically open the ULC account during an Alberta board meeting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident natural-person beneficial ownership in an unlimited-liability pass-through structure creates an opacity red flag under FINTRAC CDD (25% ownership/control rule).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO schedule with name, date of birth, country of tax residence, ownership percentage, and source-of-wealth statement; Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate of Status; copy of register of members and directors; notarized and apostilled passports; signed CRS/FATCA self-certification (Form W-8BEN-E for U.S. shareholders); latest ABCA annual return; a board resolution explaining the ULC commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency e-commerce crowdfunding proceeds (Kickstarter via Stripe/PayPal) with dispersed consumer settlement may be treated as unexplained cash-cow inflows or potential third-party funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign agreement and funding terms; Stripe/PayPal settlement statements with payout cadence; customer order ledger reconciled to bank CAMT053/051 statements; refund and chargeback policy; shipping logs (Canada Post/FedEx/UPS) for packaged dice sets; a cash-flow forecast showing monthly USD/CAD volumes and customer concentration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Epoxy resin raw-material imports from intermediary jurisdictions (e.g., bulk monomer via trading houses) may trigger trade-based money-laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier onboarding file (trade license, certificate of incorporation, bank reference, agency agreement); pro-forma invoices with HS 3907 (epoxide resins) and 9504 (games) classification; bills of lading and customs release from CBSA; Incoterms 2020 (DAP or FOB) in a written purchase contract; a COGS and margin model demonstrating genuine manufacturing cost.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) election may be misread as a zero-substance vehicle or as convincing evidence of a price-abuse pass-through arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Canadian counsel explaining the ABCA ULC structure and its U.S. check-the-box pass-through rationale; notarized acknowledgment of unlimited shareholder liability; Alberta foundry/packaging lease or utility bills; equipment purchase invoices (silicone molds, epoxy pouring stations, UV curing lamps, pressure pots); CRA Business Number and GST/HST registration certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name-only sanctions and PEP screening hits (World-Check / Refinitiv L-1) delay account opening for a low-risk entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Archived sanction-screening output for all UBOs and signatories; a dated negative-media search and explanation memo for any LPR (living person resemblance); proof of residence in non-sanctioned jurisdictions (Canada, U.S., EU); a sworn statutory declaration that the ULC has no dealings with sanctioned persons in Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, or Syria; an undertaking to submit monthly transaction monitoring reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from non-resident shareholders will be routed under either a subscription agreement (issuance of ULC shares) or a shareholder loan agreement. Comply with the following wire discipline: (a) remitter sends a SWIFT MT103 through the correspondent network with field 59 naming the ULC exactly and the beneficiary account sort/transit at the Alberta bank; (b) the ISO 20022 purpose code must be EQUI (equity) or INTR (intercompany loan), with a free-text REM field referencing 'ULC Subscription Agreement dated [date]' or the intercompany loan note; (c) all subscription proceeds will be credited to the Capital Escrow Account under a two-signature mandate, released only on resolution of closing conditions (board authorization, Alberta registration update, and UBO file completion); (d) aggregate credits equal to or above CAD 10,000 will trigger FINTRAC monitoring but require no affirmative client filing; (e) for U.S. shareholders, ensure a Form W-8BEN-E or W-9 is on file and that CRA Part XIII withholding is aligned with the treaty and section 212 exemptions; (f) no Bank of Canada authorization is required for the remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements consolidate into three clearing rails. First, consumer refunds and small raw-material reorders below CAD 10,000 are settled via ACH (U.S.), EFT (CAD), commercial cards, or Stripe/PayPal refund flows. Second, standard supplier settlements (epoxy resin, pigments, silicone, packaging) use a direct SWIFT MT103 with field 70 referencing the commercial invoice number and HS classification, combined with an intra-bank FX conversion at the same value date; two approvers must pre-authorize in the corporate banking portal. Third, capital purchases (e.g., 3D printers, industrial mixing equipment, bulk monomer above CAD 25,000) use an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued by the Canadian bank, available by payment at sight or deferred payment under MT700, governed by UCP 600 and eUCP 2.0, with Incoterms DAP; the freight-forwarder documentation pack must include a commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and certificate of origin. MT202 COV is used only for the cover transfer between correspondent banks. Consumer rails (PayPal/Stripe) must never be used as a trade-settlement channel for supplier invoices, as platform terms restrict treasury use and do not offer recourse under UCP.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts with maturities up to 12 months under the bank's master FX agreement (typically an ISDA or bilateral forward schedule)
FX swap (same-currency principal exchange with different value dates) for smoothing mismatched USD inflow and CAD outlay timing
Cross-currency swap (CAD/USD) matched to the notional amount and maturity of an intercompany shareholder loan
Vanilla CAD/USD call or put options for protecting the USD-denominated Kickstarter/Stripe inflows
Zero-cost replicating collar (buying a CAD/USD cap and selling a floor) to lock a hedging corridor on large campaign proceeds

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): not applicable for CAD in the onshore interbank market because CAD is freely deliverable; offshore NDF quotations for CAD are non-standard and not treated as a risk-appropriate treasury product

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Corporations Information Act annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (filed online through an authorized Registry Agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation, each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD $100 late-filing penalty applied after the 60-day window; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to strike the ULC from the corporate register and initiate administrative dissolution under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance of tax payable due within 2 months after year-end (3 months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation eligible for the small business deduction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; compounded daily interest on unpaid amounts; gross negligence penalty may apply for repeat or deliberate omissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, administered and collected by the Canada Revenue Agency on Alberta's behalf
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the T2 within 6 months after fiscal year-end; provincial balance of tax payable due within 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible CCPCs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Alberta late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid provincial balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; provincial interest accrues on unpaid amounts; unfiled returns may trigger arbitrary assessment and loss restriction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (Form GST34) for annual remitter status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 3 months after fiscal year-end for annual remitters; monthly or quarterly instalment filing applies if assigned by the CRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ministerial penalty of 5% of the net unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; compounded daily interest; exceeding the CAD $30,000 small-supplier threshold without registration triggers retroactive assessment, penalties, and compliance enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under section 159 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act, the ULC must appoint an auditor at its first annual general meeting and annually thereafter unless every shareholder passes a unanimous resolution to dispense with the auditor; no revenue or asset threshold applies, and audit exemption for a private ULC requires unanimity. An annual general meeting must be held within 18 months of incorporation and within 15 months of each prior AGM.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Part II ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook) is the standard framework for a private Alberta ULC; IFRS is mandatory if the ULC is a reporting issuer, offers securities to the public, or consolidates into public-group financial statements; US GAAP bridge schedules should be maintained for US check-the-box integration of the ULC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta has enacted beneficial-ownership transparency amendments, but the individuals with significant control (ISC) register regulations are not yet fully proclaimed; accordingly, no separate annual UBO filing fee is currently payable. The Alberta annual return confirms only directors and registered office. The ULC must update its members' transfer register within 15 days of any share transfer and maintain an ISC-style register at its registered office pending proclamation, if applicable to the ULC.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including share transfer history)
Register of Directors (with residential and serving addresses)
Minute Book (articles, bylaws, board minutes, shareholder resolutions)
Financial records and audit or audit-waiver resolutions (CRA minimum retention 6 years; governance retention 7 years)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000-US$9,500 per engagement, waivable by unanimous shareholder resolution for a private ULC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined federal (15%) + Alberta (8%) general corporate rate; 11% combined (9% + 2%) for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) active business income up to CAD 500,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal-Provincial Small Business Deduction ... plus 100% CCA for manufacturing equipment ...
